props.name: chromium above 25 improves in use
props.statement: Catalysts containing less than 25 atomic per cent chromium suffered a decrease in activity during use, while those containing more than 25 atomic per cent chromium improved.

props.name: chromium prevents overheating loss
props.statement: Chromium markedly prevents the loss of activity suffered by catalysts of high zinc content when exposed to temperatures somewhat above the optimum operating temperature; catalysts with a Zn:Cr molecular ratio of about 1 showed continuous improvement during extended use above the temperature of maximum activity.

props.name: cr2o3 more active than zno
props.statement: Chromium oxide has more activity than zinc oxide (both precipitated by ammonia) when allowance is made for the shrinkage of the chromium oxide: 6.8 per cent at 56,000 space velocity adjusts to an estimated 9.3 per cent at 25,000, against 6.0 per cent for zinc oxide at 25,000; chromium oxide also gave purer methanol and was superior as regards injury at high temperature and breakage.

props.name: glow only 92 cr
props.statement: Only the 92 atomic per cent chromium catalyst displayed the glow phenomenon (spontaneous temperature rises) during the synthesis tests; higher temperatures in the preliminary treatment delayed the heat effect; all three samples lost 60 per cent of volume and 45 per cent of weight.

props.name: na2co3 zno more active
props.statement: Zinc oxide precipitated by sodium carbonate is markedly more active than zinc oxide precipitated by ammonium hydroxide; the most active zinc oxide was made with a slight insufficiency of sodium carbonate.

props.name: preliminary reduction low pressure
props.statement: In large-scale operation the shrinkage would be dealt with by carrying out the preliminary reduction in simple low-pressure equipment and transferring the catalyst to the high-pressure equipment with precautions against contamination or oxidation.

props.name: product nearly pure methanol
props.statement: The liquid product was substantially pure methanol with a small percentage of water; maximum methanol contents were 96.4 to 99.8 per cent by volume except for pure zinc oxide (86) and the 92 atomic per cent chromium catalyst (79); in all cases the methanol percentage decreased with increasing operating temperature.

props.name: reactor heat capacity kept glow low
props.statement: The relatively great heat capacity of the reactor kept the maximum glow temperatures low; the effect is an indication of the frequently observed glow phenomenon.

props.name: reproducibility
props.statement: Interrupted constant-temperature runs agreed within 2 per cent; a repeat of the whole preparation and testing of pure zinc oxide differed by less than 5 per cent; the total error in conversions was probably less than 10 per cent in all cases and less than 5 per cent at higher conversions.

props.name: shrinkage increases with chromium
props.statement: Catalysts charged unreduced shrank during testing, the shrinkage increasing with chromium content, so that results late in the tests of high-chromium catalysts were at actual space velocities more than double the recorded 25,000.

props.name: table3 applies to other compositions
props.statement: The agreement of the space-velocity-adjusted Table I results with Table II indicates that the Table III space velocity vs. conversion data can be safely applied to other catalysts of the same type but of quite different composition.

props.name: trivalent chromium superior
props.statement: Catalysts prepared by methods using chromic acid (chromium trioxide) as the chromium source are much less active than those made by ammonia precipitation from the nitrates, with the chromium initially trivalent.

props.name: wall thermocouple error
props.statement: The difference between a thermocouple on the outside wall and one at the center of the catalyst was an approximately linear function of the rate of heat evolution and practically independent of temperature: about 20 °C higher outside without reaction and about 20 °C lower at 16 per cent conversion; temperature measurements outside the pressure wall are therefore uncertain.

props.name: zinc up to 25 lowers cr2o3
props.note: the authors state it is confirmed by methanol decomposition tests of Huffman and Dodge (ref. 12), cited from that paper
props.statement: Addition of zinc oxide up to about 25 atomic per cent lowers the methanol synthesis activity of a chromium oxide catalyst.

props.name: zn cr ratio 1 most active
props.statement: The most active zinc oxide-chromium oxide catalyst has an atomic ratio of zinc to chromium of around 1 (region of Zn50Cr50), not about 3 as found in the early (short) tests.

props.name: zn cr rugged active
props.statement: Mixtures of zinc and chromium oxides made by ammonia precipitation from the mixed nitrates are active and physically rugged methanol catalysts; the catalyst of maximum activity (region Zn50Cr50) produces very nearly pure methanol, appears uninjured by long use or by operation considerably above the normal temperature, and is physically rugged.

props.name: zn58cr42 resists overheating
props.statement: A preshrunk (hydrogen-reduced) Zn58Cr42 catalyst was not lowered in activity at 300 °C by 5 h at 500 °C or 6 h at 550 °C, lost activity after 600 °C and 685 °C, and was still fairly active after 20 hours at 200 to almost 400 °C above its normal operating temperature.

props.name: zn75cr25 most active short tests
props.statement: In the initial (short-time) testing the catalyst of 25 atomic per cent chromium and 75 atomic per cent zinc was the most active of the series.

props.name: stored CO-H2 testing gas (average of periodic analyses)
props.description: CO made by dehydrating formic acid with phosphoric acid, mixed with commercial electrolytic hydrogen and with CO2-free unconverted gas from the synthesis tests; compressed to about 200 atm and stored; purified before use.

props.name: catalyst 62 sodium carbonate insufficiency
props.statement: The exceptional activity of zinc oxide catalyst 62 may be due to the slight insufficiency of sodium carbonate used in its preparation (slight excess for catalysts 34 and 81).

props.name: dimethyl ether in product
props.statement: The difference between methanol content by specific gravity (higher) and by distillation may be due to dimethyl ether in the product; dimethyl ether formation could partially account for the discrepancy and for the water in the product even at 25,000 space velocity.

props.name: excess chromium most active
props.statement: The most active mixture would probably contain an excess of chromium oxide, since chromium oxide is in all respects superior to a comparable zinc oxide as a methanol catalyst.

props.name: glow in pure cr2o3
props.statement: The glow phenomenon probably also occurred with the pure chromium oxide catalyst, unobserved because of the attention given to control details at the time of that test.

props.name: higher alcohols one case
props.statement: In the one case with an indication of other materials in the product, these were probably higher alcohols.
